meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: South Korea (national unitary jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate registry distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Korean Commercial Act codification under the Civil Code tradition; Supreme Court precedents are persuasive but not binding; no separate federal or state corporate law distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Free Trade Agreement between the United States of America and the Republic of Korea (KORUS FTA, Investment Chapter)
Free Trade Agreement between the European Union and its Member States, of the one part, and the Republic of Korea, of the other part (EU-Korea FTA, Investment Chapter)
Free Trade Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China (Korea-China FTA)
Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of Japan for the Liberalisation, Promotion and Protection of Investment (Korea-Japan BIT 2003)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Republic of Korea AML/CFT and UBO framework is governed by (i) Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 19029, as amended), administered by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU); (ii) Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment (Act No. 19030); (iii) Commercial Act, Articles 543-616, governing Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) formation; (iv) the Act on Real Estate Registration under Real Name for real-asset beneficial ownership reporting; and (v) FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 as applied through Korea's 2022 mutual evaluation follow-up. Where any upstream Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) is a PRC WFOE, the PBOC/SAMR Beneficial Ownership Determination and Registration Measures (Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024) applies to that Chinese entity and mandates a Government_Only_Access disclosure level; that disclosure does not substitute for Korean AML obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner (corporate UBO) or equivalent registration record from the home-country corporate registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country corporate registry (e.g., Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations, Hong Kong Companies Registry, or analogous registrar)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille member state): original or certified true copy is notarized by an authorised notary, then an Apostille certificate is attached by the home-country designated competent authority (e.g., Secretary of State, Foreign Ministry, or specific government office); the apostilled document is submitted directly to the Korean registry or bank. Path B (non-member state): the notarized document is authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the source country, then consular-legalized by the Embassy/Consulate of the Republic of Korea in that source country. The two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (active status certificate) for the corporate UBO or a certificate of subsisting registration from the home-country registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country corporate registry or registered agent with authority to issue certificates of good standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Path A (Hague Apostille member state): certificate must be issued by the registry within 30 days before notarization, then apostilled by the home-country competent authority; no consular legalization. Path B (non-member state): registry certificate must be notarized, certified by the source-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and finally legalized by the Korean Embassy/Consulate located in that source country; chain is parallel, never combined with Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney appointing the Korean resident manager and the local incorporation agent, including express authority to file the registration and sign tax documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the ultimate beneficial owner entity, attested by the corporate secretary or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route for member states: resolution executed by directors, notarized by public notary, and apostilled by the country's designated authority; accepted directly in Korea without consular visa. Consular route for non-member states: notarized resolution must proceed through source-country ministry authentication and Korean consular legalization; no apostille may be superimposed.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter / Statute) of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, clearly stating the pharmaceutical fractionation business purpose for heparin sodium anticoagulant production and distribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public preparing the Articles, together with the founding shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Korean document: no apostille or consular legalization is required because the Articles are executed in Korea; they are notarized by the Korean notary and submitted to the District Court registry. For any foreign-language annex or originals containing foreign signatures, the apostille or consular legalization rules apply to the foreign-sealed documents only, but the two paths are mutually exclusive depending on the annex state.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (ledger bank assurance of account conduct, credit standing, and reasonable transaction history for the corporate UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principal commercial bank or credit institution of the UBO in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: the bank's authorized officer must sign and the bank seal be notarized; the notarized original then receives an Apostille from the competent authority of the bank's state and is delivered to the Korean banking counterpart. Consular path: the notarized bank letter must be authenticated by the source-country foreign ministry and then legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate; never chain the Apostille after consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport (or government-issued national identity card) of each natural-person Ultimate Beneficial Owner, with an English translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority plus a public notary in the UBO's country of residence or legalization, and a certified translator for the English translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille for member states: notary certifies passport copy and competence of the translator, then apostille attached; no consular launch required. Consular for non-member states: notarized passport copy and translation are legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate in the state of issuance; the two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be chained.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: PEP and sanctions screening protocols require exhaustive and dynamic screening of all Ultimate Beneficial Owners, directors, shareholders, and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT sanctions list, and the Republic of Korea's own Financial Transaction Reports Act designations. Each individual must be screened using name transliteration in Hangul, English, Hanja, and alternative romanization; screening must include PEP matching against 170+ jurisdictions' public officials, negative news, adverse media, and regulatory enforcement records. Any identification match triggers enhanced due diligence and mandatory suspicious transaction reporting to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit within 24 hours, and transaction bans where sanctions overlap apply.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea InterNet Registration Office (iRO / iREG) at https://www.iros.go.kr, operated by the Korean Court Registry Office, supplemented by the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) digital incorporation advisory portal for foreign investors
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean statutory doctrine requires the Yuhan Hoesa trade name to be expressed in Hangul, with an optional Hanja parenthetical and an English rendering that is a Revised Romanization of the Hangul; for example, the name Yuhan Hoesa must appear on the corporate stamp and registry filing in Hangul, and the English name shall be a direct transliteration or an internationally known registered alias. The doctrine contains four tiers of control under Articles 19-23 and 254 of the Commercial Act: (1) uniqueness and distinctiveness against pre-existing identical names in the same registry and same business type; (2) lawful composition of the legal form suffix (the LLC must be styled Yuhan Hoesa, not Jusik Hoesa); (3) prohibition of false or deceptive identification of scope, size, or nationality; and (4) prohibition of public-order-sensitive tokens. For foreign investors, the proceeds of incorporation must clearly identify the original foreign trademark or business name and its Hangul transliteration to enable cross-verification at the tax and customs phase.

stage_1.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the registry division of the competent Korean District Court within 30 days of the written rejection notice under the Korean Administrative Procedures Act. The appeal must include the proposed Hangul name, evidence of the preliminary search result, and a statement of why the name is distinctive and not deceptive, plus any ministerial approval if the rejection was based on a sensitive token. The registrar will conduct a supplementary search for identical or confusingly similar names; if the deficiency is a ministerial review, the applicant must apply to the Financial Services Commission, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, or the relevant authority and attach the approval in the registry record. If the administrative appeal is denied, the applicant may file a lawsuit with the Seoul Administrative Court within 90 days of the adverse final decision; a change to an alternative transliteration with a non-identical suffix is generally faster and more commercially practical.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not per se illegal at formation under the Korean Commercial Act, and the registered address may initially be the law firm's address for correspondence purposes. However, for a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in ISIC 3250 (chemical fractionation of low-molecular-weight heparin and manufacture of anticoagulant pharmaceutical preparations) using Letter of Credit and SWIFT wire payment rails, the National Tax Service requires an actual place of business for value-added tax registration and electronic tax invoice issuance under the Value-Added Tax Act; the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety requires a licensed GMP premises or a fully documented contract manufacturing facility; and Korean banks, in managing AML/CFT risk, will refuse a corporate bank account relying solely on a virtual office or re-mailing address. The entity must therefore maintain a physical registered business address in Korea with leases, utility records, or a compliant contract manufacturing relationship supporting commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (1) on-site compliance with the Korean signage requirement and display of the corporate registry seal in the registered office; (2) verified original lease or sublease with matching building units; (3) current electrical, water, telecommunication, and operating permit filings; (4) existence of a resident responsible person or pharmacist/manufacturing license meeting the pharmaceutical regulatory framework; (5) actual production or fractionalization records, laboratory logs, and batch records for heparin sodium; (6) power of attorney documents matching the Korean registration; (7) VAT returns and no prolonged zero-filing pattern; (8) bank statements reflecting financial activity consistent with the pharmaceutical business purpose. Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection by municipal tax, registry, or MFDS authorities within the first 18 months is 45% to 65%, with 5-10 minutes notice typically given to access the premises.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary fee schedule of the Korean Notary Public Association for company articles notarization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal and compliance fee for Stage 1 pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO identification, PEP/OFAC/UN screening, AML internal procedures and incorporation drafting

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 17219, as amended), Chapter 6 on Limited Liability Companies (Articles 287-1 through 287-66), specifically Articles 287-2, 287-3, 287-20, 287-36, 287-44 and 287-57, together with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act where any member is a non-resident; supplementary procedural rules under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act and the Registration of Real Estate and Corporation Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry Office (Court Registration Bureau) of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, administered under the Supreme Court of Korea; subsequent business registration is completed with the local District Tax Office of the National Tax Service.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa and the Application for Registration of Establishment of a Limited Liability Company, together with the paid-in capital custody certificate and statutory officer consent documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act for a Yuhan Hoesa. No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account are required. The members must fix the total contribution amount in the Articles, and the registry will require evidence of actual payment, normally by a paid-in capital custody certificate issued by a Korean bank. If contributions are made in kind, the Commercial Act requires court-appointed appraisal and, where applicable, an in-kind contribution inspection report. Foreign exchange contributions from non-resident members must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act but need not be placed in a frozen escrow account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the total contribution capital of Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company) shall be the amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation, namely KRW 100,000,000 or such higher amount as may be set out in Schedule 1 to these resolutions, allocated among the members in proportion to their respective contribution ratios. The Board acknowledges that each member's contribution has been fully subscribed and paid into the company's capital collection account, that no contribution is defective, unpaid, subject to set-off, or reserved for withdrawal, and that the Register of Members and Contributions will be maintained at the registered office in accordance with the Commercial Act. The Board hereby approves the share capital subscription documents and directs the Representative Member to countersign all contribution allocation forms and to submit the paid-in capital custody certificate to the District Court Registry together with the incorporation filing. 

RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be adopted as the address stated in Article 2 of the Articles of Incorporation, and that the lease agreement, security deposit, utilities, zoning compliance, and physical workplace arrangements for the pharmaceutical extraction facility are approved. The Representative Member is authorized to execute the lease, to deliver the landlord consent form required by the registry, and to manage all ordinary office and facility expenses. 

RESOLVED, that the principal banking institution of the Company is designated as the foreign exchange bank named in the opening banking schedule. The Representative Member, the Director of Finance, and the Company Secretary, acting jointly in any combination of two authorized signatories, are authorized to open and operate bank accounts, to sign checks, to execute SWIFT wire transfers, to issue applications for foreign exchange transactions, and to handle documentary letter of credit operations necessary for heparin sodium raw material procurement and export settlement. 

RESOLVED, that the following statutory officers are appointed: the individual designated in the Articles as Representative Member, who shall be the statutory director empowered with daily management; the individual designated as Director responsible for quality, GMP, and production; the individual designated as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer; and, where required by law or the Articles, the individual designated as Statutory Auditor. Each officer assumes office immediately, shall perform duties with fiduciary care, and shall comply with the Commercial Act, the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act, and applicable Korean corporate governance requirements. 

RESOLVED, that the officers and professional advisers of the Company are authorized to prepare and file all establishment registration forms, business registration returns, corporate tax identification applications, seal registration documents, pharmaceutical manufacturing authorization applications, Good Manufacturing Practice compliance certificates, environmental impact assessments, environmental discharge permits, Civil Defense fire safety approvals, and all related instruments, and to retain legal counsel, certified public accountants, and technical consultants as necessary to bring the Company into full statutory operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Preparation and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Name Search Center of the Supreme Court of Korea through the local District Court Registry, and a commissioned notary public authorized by the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The proposed corporate name must be checked against the court registry record to ensure it is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing legal entity. The name must include the corporate identifier Yuhan Hoesa or LLC. The incorporators must then execute the Articles of Incorporation, which must state the company name, business purpose, registered office address, total contribution capital, contribution values allocated to members, names and addresses of members and directors, duration, and statutory auditor position if required. All members and directors must personally appear or provide duly authenticated authority before the notary. The notary must certify identity, legal capacity, and consent to avoid later challenges to the formation. At least two original copies should be executed, one for the registry and one for the company records.
required_dossiers: Completed name search application
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Passport or national identification card of all members and directors
Apostilled certificate of good standing or corporate registration for any corporate member
Validated power of attorney for each authorized signatory and notarized signature certificate
Written statement of registered office address and landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search identifies a conflict, a new name must be selected and submitted in the same cycle. If the notary refuses certification because of defective identification or legal capacity, the incorporators must file corrected and apostilled identity evidence. If a provision of the Articles is contrary to the mandatory rules of the Commercial Act, the Articles must be amended and re-executed before the notary prior to any registration filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Deposit and Issuance of Paid-In Capital Custody Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Korean licensed commercial bank or foreign exchange bank supervised by the Financial Services Commission, through the bank branch designated in the incorporation schedule.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the incorporators must open a temporary subscription account in the name of the incorporators or the company in formation, as required by the bank's internal policy. Each member must deposit the full value of the contribution shown in the Articles. The bank will verify the identity and source of funds for each member, including any inward foreign exchange remittance, under the Financial Transactions Information Act and anti-money laundering obligations. Once all contributions are paid and maintained until the bank issues the certificate, the bank will issue a paid-in capital custody certificate stating the account holder, contribution amount, and date of deposit. The certificate must be retained and submitted with the establishment registration application. Funds may not be withdrawn before the registration is completed.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Passports or national identification of each subscriber
Completed bank account application and proof of foreign exchange remittance report
Beneficial ownership information forms
Bank signature card and corporate seal impression
Letter designating the account as a capital contribution account for incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank asks for enhanced due diligence because a foreign member is involved, the incorporators must supply the Economic Ownership Declaration, source-of-wealth statement, and corporate parent company documents. If the inward remittance report contains an incorrect purpose code, the bank should file a correction with the foreign exchange information system before issuing the custody certificate. If the bank declines to issue the certificate because the account was opened in the wrong name, the account must be closed and reopened in the exact name used in the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Establishment of the Yuhan Hoesa with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry Office for corporations of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, using the electronic registration information system operated by the Supreme Court of Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The filing party must submit the notarized Articles, the bank-issued paid-in capital custody certificate, statutory officer acceptance declarations, the application for establishment registration, and the corporate seal impression form. The registry examiner will verify that the company name, purpose, capital contribution figure, registered office, and director appointments are consistent and lawful. Any defect in the articles, notarization, identity, or capital payment will trigger a supplement order. The applicant must pay the registration tax and local education tax through the electronic assessment system, and after the entry is accepted, the registry will issue a certified corporate registration extract demonstrating legal personality. It is recommended that the application be submitted electronically through a licensed attorney or certified scrivener to avoid form discrepancies.
required_dossiers: Application for Establishment Registration of a Limited Liability Company
Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank paid-in capital custody certificate
Consent forms of appointed directors and statutory auditor
List of members and contribution schedule
Certified copy of lease agreement for registered office and landlord consent
Corporate seal impression report
Power of attorney and certified identification of the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplement order, the applicant must comply within two weeks by correcting the specified defects; failure to comply results in rejection of the registration. If registration is rejected, the party must correct the defects and file a new application, or appeal the rejection through the relevant civil procedure remedies. If the capital certificate is challenged, the bank must issue a corrected certificate showing the exact date, amount, and name matching the Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration, Corporate Tax Identification and Seal Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office of the National Tax Service in whose district the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after the court registration, the company must submit the Business Registration application together with the certified corporate registration extract, Articles of Incorporation, registered office lease, landlord approval, and identification of the representative director. The National Tax Service will issue the Business Registration Certificate and assign the corporate tax identification number for value added tax, corporate income tax, and withholding tax purposes. The company seal impression already registered with the court becomes the official seal for bank accounts and government filings. The company should also register an additional corporate seal or electronic certificate for e-filing if necessary. This step is essential for opening permanent operating accounts and for any subsequent pharmaceutical license applications.
required_dossiers: Application for Business Registration of a Domestic Corporation
Certified corporate registration extract issued by the court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease agreement and landlord consent
Corporate seal certificate and specimen seal
Passport or national identification of the representative member
Corporate tax entity information form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the physical office address, the company must submit a utility bill, lease registration, or floor plan proving actual use. If the filing is late, the National Tax Service may impose a penalty, and the company should file a corrective explanation and evidence of inability to file on time within thirty days to seek penalty abatement. If the corporate seal is rejected, the company must update the seal registration at the court before resubmitting the tax documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Authorization and Good Manufacturing Practice Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety of the Republic of Korea, Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Authorization Division, with on-site inspection by the regional MFDS office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company must apply for a pharmaceutical manufacturer's license under Article 31 of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act before manufacturing, fractionating, purifying, or storing heparin sodium for commercial use. The application must describe the full low-molecular-weight heparin extraction process, solvent handling, purification columns, quality control laboratories, water systems, HVAC classification, and stability program. The MFDS will review the facility design and quality management system, and will conduct a GMP inspection under Article 34(4) of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act. The authorization is site-specific and process-specific; any change in manufacturing method, cleanroom class, or critical equipment must be approved through a post-approval change management submission. Production may not begin until both the manufacturer's license and the GMP certificate are issued.
required_dossiers: MFDS Application for Pharmaceutical Manufacturer's License
Site master file describing manufacturing processes and facility layout
Floor plans with cleanroom classification and HVAC schematic
Process flow for heparin fractionation, precipitation, purification, and drying
Quality control specification and monograph for heparin sodium
GMP risk assessment and validation protocols for water, HVAC, and cleaning
Responsible pharmacist or production manager credential evidence
Environmental and fire safety preliminary approval documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MFDS issues a supplemental data request, the company must submit complete validation data within the requested period, normally thirty days. If the GMP inspection results in critical findings, the company must provide a corrective and preventive action plan and undergo follow-up inspection. If the license is rejected because of facility or quality management deficiencies, the company may file an administrative appeal and may reapply after full remediation and new construction approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Impact Assessment, Environmental Discharge Permits, Civil Defense Fire Safety, and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea, the metropolitan or provincial environmental agency, the local fire department under the National Fire Agency, and the local municipal building office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because heparin sodium manufacturing involves chemical fractionation and organic solvent use, the site must first obtain building and occupancy permits from the local municipal government and a site-use approval under the National Land Planning and Utilization Act. The factory must secure an environmental impact assessment tier determination under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act; if the floor area or site sensitivity triggers a full or small-scale EIA, the environmental impact report must be completed before construction or operation. The company must also obtain water discharge and air emission permits under the Water Environment Conservation Act and the Clean Air Conservation Act, and must register hazardous waste handling under the Wastes Control Act. Before commencement, the local fire department must issue a Fire Safety Completion Certificate after inspecting sprinklers, chemical storage, fire extinguishers, and evacuation facilities, and the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency must evaluate workplace chemical exposure controls.
required_dossiers: EIA screening application or full environmental impact assessment report
Building permit approval and structural load inspection certificates
Water discharge permit application with effluent treatment design drawings
Air emission permit application with VOC control plans
Hazardous waste handling registration and manifests
Hazardous chemical inventory and safety data sheets
Fire protection design drawings, sprinkler certificates, and evacuation plan
Occupational safety risk assessment and material safety data sheet compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Environment classifies the project as requiring a full EIA, the applicant must commission additional baseline studies and public hearings and update the environmental management plan. If the local fire marshal rejects the fire safety certificate, the company must make the required structural or fire suppression corrections and request re-inspection. If the discharge permit is provisionally denied because effluent limits exceed the calculated load, the company must revise the treatment system design and resubmit with a quantitative compliance demonstration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, Ministry of Environment, National Fire Agency, and the local municipal government responsible for building and occupancy approvals.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Pharmaceutical Manufacturer's License under Article 31 of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act and Good Manufacturing Practice Compliance Certification under Article 34(4) of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and the competent metropolitan or provincial environmental agency under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: The heparin sodium extraction plant is a physical chemical pharmaceutical manufacturing facility requiring a minimum of environmental impact assessment screening. A Full Environmental Impact Assessment is triggered when the total building floor area exceeds 10,000 square meters or the site is within an environmentally sensitive protection area; a Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment is required for projects above the statutory floor-area threshold but below the full EIA threshold; facilities below the threshold remain subject to environmental registration, water discharge permitting, and clean air emission permitting.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from heparin sodium fractionation and purification must meet the effluent quality standards under the Water Environment Conservation Act, including, for public water bodies, biochemical oxygen demand not exceeding 10 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand not exceeding 40 mg/L, total suspended solids not exceeding 10 mg/L, total nitrogen not exceeding 20 mg/L, and total phosphorus not exceeding 2 mg/L, with stricter standards applicable in designated watershed protection zones. Air emissions from solvent evaporation must meet the Clean Air Conservation Act stack and fugitive emission standards; total volatile organic compound concentration in the exhaust gas stream should generally not exceed 300 ppm with approved vapor recovery or activated carbon treatment, and the factory must comply with the Malodor Prevention Act. Hazardous waste, including spent organic solvents, filter residues, and process sludges, must be stored in sealed, bunded, leak-proof containers and transported through the officially registered hazardous waste manifest system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Applicable. The factory must obtain a Fire Safety Completion Certificate from the local fire department confirming that automatic fire detection, sprinkler coverage, chemical segregation, emergency exits, fire doors, extinguishers, and evacuation signage are installed and inspected under the Fire Services Act. The building must also pass structural load and occupancy inspections by the local municipality under the Building Act before production. Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency clearance is required under the Occupational Safety and Health Act for chemical exposure monitoring, ventilation, emergency showers, eye wash stations, personal protective equipment programs, and medical surveillance for workers handling sodium hydroxide, organic solvents, and active pharmaceutical ingredients, with documented workplace exposure control measures in place before the start of manufacturing.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic filing and registration portal: HomeTax (Hometax) at https://www.hometax.go.kr. Cross-border export clearance and customs validation are administered by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS single-window system at https://unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Korean Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company): first, complete incorporation under the Korean Commercial Act by filing with the competent district court registry and obtain the corporate registration extract; second, within 20 days after business commencement, file the statutory Application for Business Registration with the NTS district tax office that has jurisdiction over the registered office, submitting the articles of incorporation, corporate registration extract, proof of office location or lease right, identity documents of directors and the representative officer, and, if the management officer is a non-resident, a notarized power of attorney appointing a Korean tax representative; third, the NTS will assign the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as both the VAT identification number and the general corporate tax identification number. For a separate foreign non-resident entity that supplies goods or services into Korea without a domestic place of business, the foreign entity must apply for simplified foreign business-owner registration through Hometax, appoint a tax representative resident in Korea authorized to receive service process and comply with VAT filings, and obtain a simplified business registration number before making the taxable supplies, unless an exemption under the Value-Added Tax Act or an applicable tax treaty applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Korean Yuhan Hoesa is treated as a domestic corporation under the Korean Corporate Tax Act and is taxable at entity level on its worldwide income. It is not eligible for pass-through treatment and is not located in a special tax-exempt zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean domestic tax law does not provide a check-the-box election for domestic limited liability companies, and no elective hybrid-mismatch classification regime exists. The Korean International Tax Adjustment Act applies mandatory matching and controlling provisions to hybrid entities and hybrid instruments, but such rules are not elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Korean Value-Added Tax (VAT) imposed under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover exemption threshold. Every Korean business operator must register with the NTS before commencing business, regardless of expected turnover. A simplified taxpayer compliance classification is available for qualifying individual business operators with annual supplies of not more than KRW 48,000,000, but this classification does not exempt registration or the underlying VAT liability.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered business operators that issue tax invoices must issue electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax electronic tax invoice service or through an NTS-integrated ERP/API channel. The electronic tax invoice must be transmitted to the NTS no later than the day following the supply date, or the invoice issuance date if later, and the NTS performs real-time schema validation on itemised fields including supplier registration number, recipient registration number, supply value, VAT amount, and goods or service description, and then assigns an electronic transmission number. Korea does not use a separate Latin American-style anti-fraud digital stamp; instead, the NTS operates continuous cross-validation between electronic tax invoices, cash receipts for qualifying B2C retail supplies, and Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export clearance records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under the Value-Added Tax Act and its Enforcement Decree to tangible goods physically exported from Korea when the Korean exporter of record files an accepted export declaration with the Korea Customs Service, title and risk pass to a non-resident buyer, the goods are delivered outside Korea or into a recognized export route, and the export consideration is earned and settled in foreign currency. The Yuhan Hoesa low-molecular-weight heparin sodium anticoagulant crude fractionation products qualify as exported goods when shipped under a valid pharmaceutical export licence and covered by a customs-cleared export declaration naming the Korean LLC as exporter.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Accepted Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Export Clearance Certificate) issued through UNI-PASS
Commercial invoice and packing list corresponding to the customs export declaration
Purchase order, sales contract, or binding letter of credit evidencing the overseas buyer and terms of sale
Original or authenticated Bill of Lading for ocean freight, or Air Waybill for air freight, naming the Korean LLC as shipper or exporter
Foreign exchange receipt settlement confirmation or Certificate of Receipt of Export Proceeds issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing repatriation of the export proceeds

Complete API batch record and certificate of analysis for the heparin sodium anticoagulant product, required for customs and pharmaceutical export substantiation in the ISIC 3250 active pharmaceutical extraction business
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS automatically cross-matches the VAT return zero-rated export line items with Korea Customs Service export declarations and with Korean foreign exchange bank settlement reports. If the exporter cannot substantiate physical export or fails to repatriate foreign currency within the statutory 180-day settlement period, the NTS may reverse the zero-rating, assess VAT at 10% on the invoiced amount, and impose late-payment additional tax, negligence penalties, and other charges under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Fraudulent, false, or deliberately unsubstantiated zero-rating claims may subject the taxpayer to criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, including imprisonment and fines, and the NTS may apply retrospective clawback assessments covering prior statutory periods where the export documentation is found to be forged or materially misleading.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea, acting together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Foreign Exchange Information System under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a generally liberalised but tightly monitored convertibility regime. Current account transactions, including trade in goods and services, are freely convertible and may be settled in KRW or foreign currency through licensed domestic banks. Capital account transactions are also nominally liberalised, yet every inward or outward foreign exchange transaction above the reporting threshold of USD 5,000 or the KRW equivalent must be reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System unless specifically exempted. Dividend remittances and capital repatriation by foreign-invested companies are permitted subject to submission of tax payment certificates, audited financial statements, foreign exchange bank confirmation, and compliance with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Despite the absence of an ordinary surrender requirement, export proceeds must be collected before the prescribed settlement deadline and either deposited into a foreign currency account maintained with a Korean foreign exchange bank or repatriated into Korea; conversion into KRW is at the exporter's commercial discretion. The practical convertibility obstacles are therefore documentary and regulatory rather than prohibitive. Banks undertake enhanced due diligence on the ultimate beneficial owner, source of funds, intended transaction profile, and genuine commercial substance of the underlying trade. For a heparin sodium extraction company, audit trails covering the purchase of crude heparin, pharmaceutical toll conversion, and export logistics materially support both convertibility and remittance clearances. No central bank approval is required for routine FX conversion, but the entity must maintain its settlement accounts with a bank authorised as a foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and related regulations, export proceeds must be received within six months from the date of export declaration and must be either repatriated to Korea or deposited in a foreign currency deposit account held with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank. There is no statutory percentage requiring conversion to KRW; the company may keep export earnings in foreign currency. Any extension beyond six months must be justified and approved by the responsible foreign exchange bank or the relevant foreign exchange authority, and the documentary evidence should include the customs export declaration, commercial invoices, and the corresponding collection file.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Currency Investment Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / KRW Demand Deposit Account
Capital Escrow Account / Foreign Currency Investment Account and KRW Operating Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / KRW Demand Deposit Account with LC issuance capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Thin viability. Korean law does not grant fintech electronic money institutions the status of a foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, so offshore EMIs cannot independently clear KRW, open onshore won deposit accounts, register foreign investment, or issue Korean commercial letters of credit. Digital EMI platforms such as cross-border payment processors may be used only as secondary collection or pre-funding conduits that push funds through SWIFT into the entity's domestic corporate account. Any attempt to use an unauthorised EMI as the primary account for customer collections, vendor disbursements, or capital injections would create incomplete transaction-purpose information and expose the company to enhanced AML/CFT scrutiny. The compliant treasury architecture is therefore domestic Korean bank accounts as the regulated settlement rail, with EMIs limited to customer-facing collection conveniences and never serving as KRW clearing infrastructure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance at a Korean branch or overseas branch of a major Korean bank is generally required for the statutory director and beneficial shareholders. Remote video KYC may be accepted by some tier-1 banks if passport certification, notarised articles of incorporation, corporate resolution, apostilled powers of attorney, and a full beneficial ownership chart are presented, but consular proxy account opening without direct banking appointment is not uniformly recognised. The board must designate a resident foreign exchange reporting contact or registered business agent to manage FEIS filings, and the bank will conduct an enhanced KYC interview covering the crude heparin purchase chain, anticoagulant production capacity, buyer distribution network, expected monthly settlement volumes, and the commercial substance of the Korean LLC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership is held through a non-resident holding company in a jurisdiction without strong FATF compliance and with no track record in pharmaceutical manufacturing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarised and apostilled corporate organisation chart, current share register, certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, notarised passports of all natural-person beneficial owners, three years of audited financial statements from the ultimate parent, tax residence certificates, bank reference letters from the ultimate parent's home bank, an independent adverse media and sanctions screening report, and a sworn statement explaining the source of wealth and source of funds for the Korean entity formation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Import invoices for crude heparin and export invoices for heparin sodium derivatives show significant quantity, freight cost, or unit-price variance, creating a red flag for invoice manipulation or trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble a transaction file containing the master purchase contract and export off-take agreements, supplier and buyer commercial invoices, packing lists, bill of lading or air waybills, Korean customs import/export declarations, freight forwarder confirmations, third-party laboratory assay certificates, batch production records, pharmacopoeia certificates of analysis, and the precise toll conversion or chemical fractionation yield calculation proving the mass-balance relationship between crude heparin input and finished sodium heparin output.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected inbound payments from multiple Korean wholesale pharmacies and overseas hospital distributors have not been pre-disclosed, creating uncertainty about the true counterparty network
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a pre-screened customer KYC register for each counterparty with legal name, tax number, beneficial ownership, business licence, distribution agreement, expected annual volumes, product pricing schedule, and standing payment instructions. Each customer must be sanctions-screened and risk-rated, and the company must provide the bank with the latest signed pharmaceutical supply agreements, licence confirmations under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act, and institutional purchase orders to evidence the legitimate trade flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The non-resident shareholder will inject foreign currency capital after formation but before material operations, raising concern about round-tripping, disguised lending, or layering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File the inward foreign direct investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act before remittance, provide the bank with the investor's board resolution approving capital injection, an audited or bank-verified source of funds statement, the investor's latest financial statements, notarised identification documents, the SWIFT MT103 remittance reference linked to the FDI report number, and the Korean bank's foreign investment registration certificate confirming the capital contribution, followed by a KRW capital verification record before operating disbursements commence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident investor must first deliver the inward foreign direct investment report to the chosen foreign exchange bank or through the Foreign Exchange Information System and obtain a report reference number. The remittance should be sent by SWIFT MT103 to the bank-designated foreign currency investment account, with the payment narration clearly citing the FDI report number, the Korean LLC name, and the purpose of share capital acquisition. On receipt, the bank will verify the identity of remitter and beneficiary, confirm the remittance matches the reported amount, register the foreign investment, and issue a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate. After capital verification, funds may be converted at the bank's prevailing market rate and transferred into the basic KRW operating account. Retain the original MT103, bank advice, FDI report confirmation, board resolution, and certificate of foreign investment registration for future dividend remittance or capital repatriation audits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for the purchase of crude heparin and processing materials will operate over SWIFT MT103 direct wires for small and medium value payments, commercial letters of credit issued or confirmed by a Korean tier-1 bank for larger documented supply contracts, and documentary collections on D/P or D/A terms for repeat low-risk suppliers and buyers. All outward payments above the reporting threshold require FEIS filing and supporting documents such as the import or export contract, customs declaration, bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of analysis. The Korean bank will validate the transaction description so that the purpose code is consistent with trade in chemical pharmaceuticals. For high-value crude heparin procurement, the company may consider an irrevocable confirmed LC with the Korean bank as issuing bank to protect the supply chain.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD and KRW/EUR forward foreign exchange contracts executed with a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank, permitted only when the notional amount is backed by documented export or import exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) transacted only with a foreign exchange bank and supported by real demand evidence such as trade orders, LC exposure, or foreign currency debt; speculative uncovered NDF positions are prohibited for non-financial corporations
KRW/USD or KRW/EUR currency swaps limited to matching committed trade cash flows or capital liabilities, with the notional amount capped at the contractually expected inflow or outflow

Plain vanilla currency options allowed solely for hedging commercial exposure, not for directional trading, and subject to the bank's underlying transaction verification and FEIS reporting requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporation income tax final return with closing financial statements for the calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea, via HomeTax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after December 31 fiscal year-end; due no later than March 31 of the following year (next working day if March 31 falls on a non-business day)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% additional tax on unreported or understated taxable income, 40% additional tax for fraudulent concealment, KRW 200,000 to KRW 5,000,000 filing default penalty, and 0.022% daily late-payment interest from the original due date; persistent delinquency after formal NTS demand notices may lead to cancellation of business registration and court-ordered administrative strike-off or dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate tax intermediate prepayment return and remittance (first-half annual corporate tax prepayment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year, due by August 31 of the current fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% additional tax on the unpaid intermediate prepayment plus 0.022% daily late-payment interest; chronic failure to file or pay may trigger compulsory collection, tax lien, business registration cancellation, and administrative strike-off by the registry court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surcharge return equal to 10% of corporation income tax (local inhabitant tax on corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local tax collection authority of the Si/Gun/Gu where the head office is registered, filed through the local tax e-filing system (WeTax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporation tax final return; due by March 31 of the year following a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% additional tax on unreported local corporate income tax surcharge, 0.022% daily late-payment interest, and compulsory collection by the municipal authority; continued non-payment may result in seizure of assets and a request to the court for corporate dissolution or strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax preliminary and final returns for the four VAT filing periods in a calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January-March preliminary return due April 25; January-June final return due July 25; July-September preliminary return due October 25; July-December final return due January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% additional tax on understated output VAT, 10% additional tax on overstated input VAT credits, and 0.022% daily late-payment interest; repeated non-filing or non-payment after NTS enforcement demand can trigger business registration cancellation and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular general meeting of members approving annual financial statements; for audit-mandated companies, filing of the independent auditor's report and audited financial statements with the financial regulator
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system for audit-mandated entities; meeting minutes and resolutions are kept at the registered office and need not be filed unless they involve registered modifications
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The regular general meeting must be convened within 3 months after fiscal year-end, by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year; audited financial statements must be filed with FSS within 2 weeks after approval by the general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: For audit-mandated entities, failure to appoint an auditor or to file audited financial statements within the statutory period is subject to civil fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, including fines up to KRW 50,000,000; the NTS may reject tax-effective financial statements, and persistent failure can result in court-ordered filing, dissolution, or administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested company change and status report; annual beneficial owner confirmation response to financial institutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA or a designated foreign-exchange bank; banking institutions for AML/UBO annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days of any foreign-investor equity transfer, change of foreign investor identity, foreign investment ratio change, or change of registered head office information; UBO confirmation must be provided at least annually when requested by the entity's financial institution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted Foreign Investment Promotion Act change reports may attract administrative fines up to KRW 10,000,000 and loss of tax or foreign-investment benefits; AML UBO non-response may lead to bank account restrictions and foreign-exchange sanctions; persistent non-compliance may be escalated to the registry court for administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent certified CPA audit is legally compulsory when the prior fiscal year-end balance sheet shows total assets exceeding KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000); when the entity is a listed or FSS-registered public company; when the company is a financial company, financial holding company, or other company designated by the FSS; or when the Financial Supervisory Service issues a public-interest audit order. Revenue and headcount are not standalone audit triggers for a private non-financial Yuhan Hoesa. A Yuhan Hoesa with total assets below KRW 12,000,000,000 that is not otherwise regulated may file unaudited financial statements with its corporate tax return. Group audit consolidation applies when the combined total assets of parent and subsidiaries exceed the same KRW 12,000,000,000 statutory threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) is mandatory for audit-mandated, listed, and financial-sector entities; Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) including the SME Accounting Standards is permitted for non-listed and non-audit-mandated private Yuhan Hoesa companies; financial statements must be prepared in Korean won under the Korean commercial bookkeeping system.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa must report changes in foreign investment details, including any transfer of equity or change in foreign investor shareholding, to MOTIE through KOTRA or a designated foreign-exchange bank within 30 calendar days of the triggering event. There is no standalone annual UBO register filing fee, but under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and FATF-aligned Korean AML rules, financial institutions must verify beneficial ownership at least annually; the company must provide updated beneficial owner information within 30 days of any shareholding transfer and must respond to each annual bank confirmation request.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500-1,500 per year for registered-office and address services in Seoul; USD 1,200-3,000 per year for outsourced corporate secretarial and annual filing administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 18,000-45,000 for a mandatory K-IFRS statutory audit; USD 5,000-12,000 for a voluntary CPA review or agreed-upon procedures for an audit-exempt Yuhan Hoesa

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9%-24% progressive: KRT 9% on tax base up to KRW 200M; 19% on KRW 200M-20B; 21% on KRW 20B-300B; 24% above KRW 300B. Local income surtax of 10% on the national corporate tax is also separately imposed.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory patent box for standard heparin fractionation; available incentives include the corporate R&D tax credit under the Special Tax Treatment Control Law (STTCL) at 20%-50% of qualifying R&D expenses, tax holidays for foreign-invested ultra-high-tech businesses in Free Economic Zones, and temporary tax reduction for medical/pharmaceutical infrastructure investment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate tax coat of arms Form 1-1 / Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return electronically filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing portal (hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual with two statutory interim prepayment instalments during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final return must be filed within three months after the fiscal year-end (31 March for calendar-year entities); foreign corporations may obtain a one-month extension with approval of the district tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, legal entity name, headquarters address, fiscal year, and shareholder classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mark the entity as a domestic Korean private limited company (Yuhan Hoesa). Disclose all non-resident shareholders and indicate whether the Korean operation is a branch of a foreign entity with a taxable Permanent Establishment (PE).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement reconciling accounting net income to taxable income by adding back non-deductible expenses and deducting tax-exempt items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled entities must add back intercompany management fees, royalties, and interest that are excessive or not backed by transfer pricing documentation. Deny deduction for expenses allocated to the foreign headquarters unless a valid cost-sharing arrangement under AOA/BEPS principles is maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 20 - Tax Base and Loss Carryforward Application
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the final corporate tax base after deducting net operating loss carryforwards within the statutory 10-year limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean Yuhan Hoesa incurred losses attributable to a foreign parent's captive manufacturing arrangement, carryforward is accepted only if the entity has a real economic substance and the loss has an arm's-length explanation. Substantial risk of denial exists for shell-like Korean entities with no local employees or factory ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 30 - Income Tax Calculation at Progressive Rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 9%-24% national tax schedule, followed by the 10% local income tax surtax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned pharmaceutical extraction entities must attach detailed calculation for Korean-sourced heparin fractionation revenue. If a PE exists, exclude only profits properly allocated to the foreign office under OECD profit attribution rules. Misallocation attracts transfer pricing correction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of cross-border intercompany sales, purchases, royalties, interest, and service transactions with non-resident related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report every transaction with the foreign heparin supply-chain affiliates. If aggregate cross-border related-party transactions equal or exceed KRW 5 billion, attach the Local File, Master File, and the annual transfer pricing report. Failure to disclose exposes the entity to up to a 30% TP assessment surcharge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 50 - Foreign Tax Credits and Treaty Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of foreign tax credits for taxes paid abroad and the use of bilateral tax treaty deductions on domestic source income paid to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean entity must claim treaty relief on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties using Form 'Tax Treaty Income Tax Exemption / Reduction Application' submitted concurrently with the tax return. The non-resident recipient must produce a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership declaration from the jurisdiction of residence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 20% of the tax payable for unfaithful returns, rising to 40% where the omission is fraudulent; daily late-payment surcharge accrues at 0.02%-0.03% per day and is uncapped. False international transaction reporting triggers an additional 10% civil penalty and a 30% transfer pricing adjustment surcharge. Criminal prosecution is mandatory for tax fraud exceeding KRW 300 million of understated income.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate effective rate: 20% corporate income tax withholding under the Corporate Income Tax Act on dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-resident corporations, plus 2% local income tax surtax (an additional 10% of the 20% national withholding tax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, a non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its country of residence; (2) complete and submit the Korean form 'Application for Income Tax Exemption/Reduction Under Tax Treaty' to the NTS before payment; (3) provide a beneficial ownership certificate demonstrating that the ultimate recipient is not a conduit or pass-through entity; and (4) if relief is denied or not applied before payment, file a 5-year refund claim with the Korean district tax office. For the Korea-Japan context, dividends are generally cut to 10%-15%, and to 5% if the recipient is a directly and substantially held corporate shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate on outbound royalties and intercompany interest is 22% (20% national + 2% local surtax). Under most Korean DTAs, interest is reduced to 10%-15%, and industrial royalties (including heparin manufacturing know-how) are reduced to 10%-15%, provided the payee is the beneficial owner and the technology is not leased through a scheme of tax avoidance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5 billion aggregate cross-border related-party transactions during the fiscal year, or if the global consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and the Korean entity has any reportable cross-border transaction with a related party; both cases require preparation of the Local File, Master File, and annual transfer price report.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has no general Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) equal to Jersey/BBO regimes, but the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs (LICTAA) require real substance over another legal formalisation. Korean tax authorities may re-characterise contracts and re-allocate profits to the jurisdiction where the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA), the sourcing personnel, risk control, and strategic decisions are actually exercised. The heparin fractionation plant in Korea must prove ownership of the raw heparin inventory, factory laborers, quality control staff, and procurement decision-making; otherwise the NTS will pierce the Shanghai-Tokyo-Korea contractual veil and allocate at least the local factory return to Korea.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Transfer Pricing Manipulation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: KR_YUHANGHOESA invoices its intercompany supply of chemically fractionated low-molecular-weight heparin at an artificially low gross margin, allowing the foreign parent to capture residual profits while the Korean entity still files a loss. The annual related-party disclosure schedule deliberately omits the full volume of the cross-border heparin purchases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 9 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, the company faces imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of up to 2 times the evaded tax; on top of that, the NTS imposes a 20% unfaithful return penalty, a 40% fraudulent return penalty, and a daily late-payment surcharge. Transfer pricing adjustment adds an extra 30% assessment surcharge on the corrected taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts pierce the corporate veil where the Yuhan Hoesa is used as a pure instrument to commit tax evasion. Directors are jointly and severally liable for the entire underpaid tax, penalties, and interest. If a director faces a tax arrear of more than KRW 500 million and deliberately hides assets, the NTS will list the director on the Korean High-Risk Internship lister, approve a travel ban, and refer the case to the Prosecutor's Office for criminal prosecution with a recommendation of imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The non-resident ultimate owner interposes a zero-substance Singaporean or Jersey intermediary to receive Korean heparin royalties and residual dividend flow, claiming the reduced dividend DTA rate of 5%, but has no officers, no accounts, no office, and no legal decision-making ability. The Korean entity also signs falsified royalty agreements for technology that is already embedded in the Korean factory.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML Trade-Based Money Laundering in Cross-Border Heparin Operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity structure was formed to receive raw heparin crude from Unregulated Middle Eastern suppliers via a Hong Kong intermediary, raising import prices by 35% with fake letters of credit, then transferring the inflated gross profit to the intermediary using Korean bank wire under SWIFT. The funds do not return to the Yuhan Hoesa. The beneficial ownership of the intermediary is hidden through bearer shares.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korea's Financial Information Analysis Act (FIU) and the Proceeds of Crime Act reward guilty financial institutions and individuals with imprisonment of up to 5 years and criminal fine up to KRW 30 million; Korean customs laws impose anti-export transfer pricing penalties and VAT evasions up to 10 times the understated tax value. The Korea Customs Service additionally treats mis-invoiced heparin crude as customs violations, triggering forfeiture of goods and revocation of the pharmaceutical license under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false L/C invoices or who are functionally responsible for Korean money transfers face personal criminal liability under Article 3 of the Proceeds of Crime Act and the Violent and Poisonous Crime Act. The legal veil is pierced when the diverted funds are used for the personal enrichment of the director; in such a case, the director is required to restitute the full amount, is blacklisted by the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit, is placed on the NTS non-filing watchlist, and is subject to immigration ban and extradition proceedings.
